slides.description: Full-screen opening shot of a colorful top-down city map with the title “CAPITAL SYNDICATE” and subtitle “Financial Reality Engine.” Show the player driving between lively buildings, with a bold progress bar reading “$0 → $10M” and floating route icons for Day Job, Stocks/Crypto, Casino, Real Estate, Fishing, and Dark Web. Add a small callout: “Every building is a playable minigame—not a menu.”
slides.narration: What if GTA had a finance obsession? In Capital Syndicate, you live inside an open-world money machine and build toward ten million dollars any way you want—from a day job and trading to casino bets, real estate, fishing, or crossing into scams and black-market deals.

slides.description: A fast three-panel action montage: left, the player’s car drifting through city streets; center, bright casino tables showing Blackjack, Poker, Slots, and Russian Roulette; right, red police lights chasing the player, followed by a jail screen with three large options: “Bribe,” “Talk,” and “Escape.” Use motion lines, chips, sirens, and an arrow labeled “crime → consequence → comeback.”
slides.narration: The fun is highly visual: drive across the city, play risky casino minigames, and test how far the criminal path can take you. Go too public and the police chase you—then jail becomes another game, where you can bribe, talk, or break your way out.

slides.description: A large smartphone UI dominates the slide. Show three stacked features: an AI-generated Social/X post triggering an upward stock chart; a portrait grid of historical-figure NPCs with chat bubbles and a heart/date icon; and an AI Assistant screen answering, “How does short-selling work?” with a clear response. Add the label “AI is part of the game loop.”
slides.narration: AI is not just behind the scenes here. An in-game social feed can move stock prices, historical-figure NPCs can chat and even date you through live conversations, and your smartphone assistant can answer almost any question while you play.

slides.description: A clean, game-like milestone ladder spans the screen: “$50K → $250K → $1M → $5M → $10M,” with the final $10M node glowing and labeled “REAL WIN CONDITION.” Place a smaller, faded badge beyond it reading “$1B FLEX GOAL — OPTIONAL BRAGGING RIGHTS,” with a crossed-out “not required” note. Include small icons for trading, work, casino, property, and crime feeding into the ladder.
slides.narration: The real objective is a tiered wealth ladder: fifty thousand, two-fifty, one million, five million, and finally ten million dollars. A billion is only an optional flex goal for players who want to keep going—it is not the win condition.

slides.description: Show a stylized command-center diagram titled “10 SPECIALIST AI AGENTS,” with ten labeled nodes around a central game build: Producer, Game Designer, World Builder, Gameplay Engineer, Art Director, Visual Polish, Technical Artist, Audio Director, Writer, and QA Tester. Use arrows showing handoffs from planning to implementation to live-browser verification, plus a footer: “Narrow roles. Coordinated output. Human product owner.”
slides.narration: The project is also a lesson in agentic development. Ten specialized AI agents handle production, design, world-building, code, art, audio, writing, and QA—each with a narrow job—instead of asking one generalist assistant to do everything.

slides.description: A countdown banner reads “9–10 DAYS LEFT,” above a storyboard of the next feature: 1) a cinematic prison opening explaining why the player is locked up, 2) three prison minigames with clue tokens, 3) clues combine into an escape route, 4) the player emerges into the main city. Add a second track labeled “Polish Pass” with icons for economy, minigames, NPCs, and UI, and a note: “Prison world ships first; polish flexes to time.”
slides.narration: With nine to ten days left, the next major addition is a prison tutorial world. An opening revenge story leads into about three clue-based minigames, whose solution unlocks the escape into the city, followed by a focused polish pass across everything already shipped.
